cycle1.result: Average compliance across the three previous cycles used as comparator (figures not given).

cycle1.result: Baseline cardio-metabolic assessment in 50–65%; less than 15% at 3–6 months. Body weight and blood pressure documented at 3–6 months in 15% and 2.5% respectively. Collaboration with GP for annual health check 78–100%.

audits.title: Has vitamin D had its day? An audit of vitamin D, prolactin and HBA1C monitoring over one year in an in-patient secure service
audits.standard: Best practice: at least annual HbA1c and prolactin for all; vitamin D only if symptomatic of deficiency
audits.setting: Five in-patient secure wards (medium and low secure, including Northside House)

cycle1.result: 100% tested on the medium secure unit, but vitamin D tested without documented clinical indication; on the other units prolactin and HbA1c were least measured (18% male LSU, 23% female ward); vitamin D testing 38% female ward and 18% male ward.

audits.intervention: Recommended adding prolactin and HbA1c to pre-CPA physical screens and stopping vitamin D testing without symptoms.
audits.other_findings: The unit with a dedicated physical health team scored 100%; prolactin levels were highest on male medium secure wards.

audits.title: Could a Virtual Clinic Improve the Quality of Physical Health Monitoring for Safe Antipsychotic Prescribing in an Older Adult Community Mental Health Team (CMHT)? Encouraging Preliminary Results From a CMHT in Wales
audits.standard: NICE and Royal College of Psychiatrists guidance on physical health monitoring for antipsychotic prescribing
audits.setting: Older Adult Community Mental Health Team, South Wales

cycle1.result: Lifestyle advice 0%, physical observations 3%, blood tests 3%, ECG 3% of eligible patients; 0% had full monitoring as per guidance; mean overall compliance per patient 9%.

audits.intervention: Local protocol, staff education, a junior-doctor-led virtual physical health monitoring clinic and a phlebotomy/ECG pathway.

cycle2.result: Mean overall compliance per patient 69% (vs 9% baseline); complete monitoring as per guidance reached 50% in January 2023; bloods and ECG done in 67%; trained staff 100%.

audits.setting: Community mental health team, Glasgow

cycle1.result: 60% up to date with blood tests; 28% had an up-to-date ECG; poor documentation of smoking, alcohol and weight and of interventions offered.

audits.title: An Audit of Metabolic Monitoring Compliance in Patients Initiated on Antipsychotics Across General Adult Wards in the East Midlands
audits.standard: Lester Tool: baseline BP, HbA1c/glucose, lipids, lifestyle review and weight within one week of initiation, then weekly weight for six weeks
audits.setting: Two male and two female general adult inpatient wards, East Midlands

cycle1.result: Baseline BP 89.5%, HbA1c/glucose 65.8%, lipids 57.9%, lifestyle review 55.3%, weight 36.8%; 5.9% had full weekly weight follow-up and 41.2% none within six weeks.

audits.intervention: Recommended awareness of baseline bloods, electronic record alerts for weekly weights and a refusal drop-down, and re-audit.
audits.other_findings: Reasons for non-compliance were poorly documented; risperidone most prescribed.

audits.standard: Physical health monitoring and intervention standards of the National Audit of Schizophrenia 2021 and National Clinical Audit of Psychosis 2022 (75% standard); Lester UK tool; local target 80% after interventions
audits.setting: Mid and North Early Intervention in Psychosis service, Hampshire and Isle of Wight NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 54/118 identified as high risk. Monitoring of smoking, alcohol, illicit substances, BMI, blood pressure, lipids and glucose exceeded the 75% standard. audits.standard: BNF annual monitoring of weight, glucose/HbA1c, lipids and blood pressure: 100% with three or more of four monitored; 80% monitored for each measure
audits.setting: General practice, West Midlands

audits.title: Audit of Pre-Treatment Baseline Investigations for Patients Started on Atypical Antipsychotics – Department of Psychiatry, Gulab Devi Teaching Hospital, Lahore
audits.standard: Recommended baseline physical, laboratory and additional investigations before starting atypical antipsychotics
audits.setting: Psychiatry department inpatients, Gulab Devi Teaching Hospital, Lahore

cycle1.result: Weight/BMI 64%; blood pressure 28%; waist 0%; CBC 56%; LFTs and RFTs 52%; glucose/HbA1c 44%; lipids 48%; CPK and prolactin 0%; ECG 40%; pregnancy test 0. Combined compliance about 29%.

audits.intervention: Staff education, standardised baseline investigation checklists, visual reminders and better coordination with laboratory and ECG services.

cycle2.result: Weight/BMI 68%; blood pressure 76%; waist 48%; CBC 100%; LFTs 88%; RFTs 84%; glucose/HbA1c 76%; lipids 60%; CPK 48%; prolactin 60%; ECG 68%; pregnancy test 88%. Combined compliance 68%.

audits.other_findings: Physical assessments improved from 30.7% to 64%, laboratory from 36% to 76.6% and additional investigations from 20% to 62% over a two-month prospective audit.
